title: libpod: switch sqlite state backend to WAL mode
body:
Under heavy container churn, the SQLite state DB can get corrupted with "database disk image is malformed" due to page 1 freelist header conflicts under the default rollback journal mode (#29721).

To address this:
- Set `_journal_mode=WAL` in the SQLite connection string. This avoids writing directly to page 1 on every transaction and relies on SQLite's shared-memory locking.
- Limit max open connections on the state db handle to 1 to prevent multiple internal goroutines/threads from cycling connection file descriptors.
- Run a best-effort `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` on `SQLiteState.Close()`.
- Add a unit test checking that the database actually opens in WAL mode.

Fixes #29721

comments.body: [NON-BLOCKING] Packit jobs failed. @podman-container-tools/packit-jobs please check. Everyone else, feel free to ignore.

Max connections to 1 sounds like a step too far. Yes, it guarantees concurrency is safe, but it will murder our performance. I would try with just WAL mode and see if that's sufficient to fix things, given recent improvements in WAL locking.
